assumptions.obligation: No request (i_a_valid = 0) while rst_ni is asserted
No request in the first cycle after reset release
TL-UL host rule: a_valid held and all A-channel signals (incl. instr type and integrity flip) stable while a_valid=1 and a_ready=0
Requests at offset 0x200 and above are not used
Writes with i_a_instr = 1 are not used

The combined ALERT_TEST write (fatal_fault=1 with regwen=0) is not used: any aligned word write to ALERT_TEST whose mask reaches lanes 0 and 3 (full-mask PutFullData or PutPartialData with mask[0]&mask[3]) with good integrity does not have data[0]=1 and data[31]=0; malformed/byte/flipped writes stay legal
Any write request to CFG0, TIMER_V_LOWER0 or TIMER_V_UPPER0 only while CTRL.active_0 = 0 (no CTRL write in flight)
Timer not activated while a write to CFG0 / TIMER_V_* is still in flight

notes: CHK-008 (mask 4'b1011, a_size 0, PutFullData at 0x000): NOT added as an assumption. TL-T3.1.3.4-02 says project hosts 'should not' use non-contiguous masks, but this block's own rule RT-4.1-05 explicitly says the test bench may send TL-UL error cases including bad size or mask as legal stimulus, and TL-T3.1.3.5-03 / RT-4.1-06 require the device to answer them with d_error = 1. The counterexample is on legal stimulus; the stimulus checker nnc_chk_tbhost.sv (bad_mask) is stricter than the specification and should be relaxed instead. Related triage items: (a) the checker's ban on any write of data 0x1 to word 0x000 is stronger than RT-8-15. ENV-07 was widened only to effective writes that reach both the fatal_fault lane (0) and the regwen lane (3), i.e. PutPartialData word writes with mask[0]&mask[3] as well as full-mask writes, which are also the combined write. (b) Adopted: RT-8-03 restricts writes to CFG0/TIMER_V_* while active, and the spec does not guarantee that partial-mask word writes (e.g. mask 0111 to CFG0) have no effect, so ENV-08/ENV-10 now track any write request to those words. Item (c) of the triage text was truncated and could not be assessed.
